pr_body:
Always print C# unhandled exceptions to the console (which will also add them to the log if logging is enabled).

Closes #54389
pr_comments:
From what I understand (correct me if I'm wrong):

- Exception is printed to stdout: ✔️
- Exception is displayed in the Godot debugger errors list: ✔️
- Exception is printed to the Output panel: ❌ **(this PR wants to address this)**

If this is the case then I don't think this is the right fix as it will cause the exception to be printed twice in stdout.
A better solution could be to replace existing `mono_print_unhandled_exception` calls with this `ERR_PRINT`. But I don't know how that would look in terminals and if editors/IDEs will be able to recognize the paths to highlight them as hyperlinks (I don't know if this is done currently, just something worth checking).

In any case, this shouldn't be done from `debug_send_unhandled_exception_error` as the only purpose of this function is to send the error to the Godot editor debugger.
After a second look, this seems to only print the exception name and message while excluding the stack frames. It wouldn't be too bad to print this to stdout then in addition to the full exception text that's already being printed.
However, I don't consider the exception name and message alone to be of much utility if you can't see the stack frames. I would expect one of the following:
- Clicking the error in the output panel redirects me to the error in the debugger errors list, where I can see the stack frames.
- The stack frames are includes in the Output panel, but they are hidden by default and you can unfold to see them.
The point of this was to print the C# exception so that it gets written to the log. If all you have is the log, you can't get the stack trace from the debugger and I agree without the stack trace the exception is not very useful.

What this PR is suppose to address is printing exceptions to the log, so when players get a crash they can send the log to the developer and the log actually contains useful information.

This is not the right way to do that, as you explained. The `mono_print_unhandled_exception` method prints to **stdout**, as you'd expect, but **stdout** is not written to the log. I don't see a way to make mono print using Godot's [Loggers](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed300d7be536b1ec325ba77521eceee73dd0e5fb/core/os/os.cpp#L83) so I'm closing this.

issue_context.title: mono - Exceptions are not logged.
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v3.3.3.stable.mono.

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

If you enable file logging in project settings, the log files are successfully created at the given location. However these logs are completely useless, since no exception is recorded in them.

Every log file which was created on my system contains the same data:

"Godot Engine v3.3.3.stable.mono.official.b973f997f - https://godotengine.org
OpenGL ES 2.0 Renderer: GeForce MX150/PCIe/SSE2
OpenGL ES Batching: ON
 
Mono: Log file is: '[log poath]'"

No exceptions recorded, even if the program crashes with an obvious exception. 

I've attached a simple project to demonstrate the issue. 

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a project

- Enable file logging

- Throw an exception

- Check the log

### Minimal reproduction project

[TestLogging.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/7442942/TestLogging.zip)
comments: Sorry, I actually agree that C# exceptions should be logged just like any other error.

> Sorry, I actually agree that C# exceptions should be logged just like any other error.

No probs. Probably I wasn't crystal clear in my proposal. Normally I'm not throwing exceptions deliberately, exceptions just happen unfortunately, because my code is not perfect. In the demo project I deliberately threw an exception to demonstrate what's happening when an exception happens naturally. If you see what I mean. 

Normally I don't use the keyword "throw" in my godot project, is what I mean. :)
This is still reproducible on 4.2.1 according to https://forum.godotengine.org/t/why-are-engine-error-messages-not-in-log-file/46768.
